THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 12.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.947/2012  3  2025:KER:25105  JUDGMENT Dated this the 12th day of March, 2025
The 3rd respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No.1797/2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kottayam is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

sentences.text: The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 3.10.2002.

According to the petitioner, on 3.10.2002 at about 2.10 p.m., while he was travelling in a jeep bearing registration No.KL-K-7173 from Vandiperiyar to Mlamala, driven by the 1st respondent, he lost control over the jeep and as such it hit against a bus bearing registration No.KL- 5C-9603 and as a result of which he sustained injuries.
3.
The 1st respondent is the driver/, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the jeep.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending jeep.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is 2025:KER:25105 Rs.1,00,000/-.

4. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 1 st respondent, awarded a compensation of Rs.19,570/- and directed the 3 rd respondent/insurer to pay the same and further permitted the 3 rd respondent to recover the same from the 2nd respondent.
5. Aggrieved by the above awarded of the Tribunal, the 3 rd respondent preferred this appeal.
During the pendency of the appeal, the 2nd respondent died and additional respondents 4 to 7 are the legal heirs of 2nd respondent/ the owner of the jeep.

6. Heard Sri. George Cherian, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri. Shaji Thomas, the learned Counsel for the Additional respondents.
7.

The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant would argue that the petitioner was a gratuitous passenger in a private jeep which was covered only by a liability only policy and as such the Tribunal was not justified in mulcting the liability on the insurer and thereafter permitting them to recover from the 2nd respondent.

8. Though Sri Shaji Thomas, learned counsel represented 2025:KER:25105 additional respondents 4 to 7, no convincing arguments were advanced to sustain the impugned award passed by the Tribunal directing the 3 rd respondent to pay the compensation.

9. The learned Senior Counsel has relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Shimla v. Tilak Singh and Others [(2006) 4 SCC 404], in which it is specifically held that gratuitous passenger carried in a private vehicle is not covered under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Shimla v. Tilak Singh and Others [(2006) 4 SCC 404]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In paragraph 21, the Apex Court held that:
"21.

In our view, although the observation made in Asha Rani's case (supra) were in connection with carrying passengers in a goods vehicle, the same would apply with equal force to gratuitous passengers in any other vehicle also.

Thus, we must uphold the contention of the appellant-insurance company that it owed no liability toward the injuries suffered by the deceased Rajinder Singh who was a pillion rider, as the insurance policy was a statutory policy, and hence it did not cover the risk of death of The National Insurance C O. Ltd vs Sunny Thomas on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53392504/
3 or bodily injury to gratuitous passenger."
10.

sentences.text: On a perusal of Exhibit B1 policy, it can be seen that there is specific endorsement in it to the effect that it is only a 'liability policy'.
The petitioner has no case that he was a driver or employee of the owner of the jeep.
Therefore, the only conclusion that can be arrived is 2025:KER:25105 that he was a gratuitous passenger in the jeep, which is a private vehicle.
In this case, there is no valid policy to cover a gratuitous passenger and as such the Tribunal was not justified in mulcting the liability on the 3rd respondent.
11. In the above circumstances, the appeal is liable to be allowed and the impugned award to the extent it directed the 3 rd respondent to pay the compensation, is liable to be set aside.
12. In the result, this appeal is allowed.
The impugned Award to the extent it directed the 3rd respondent to pay the compensation to the petitioner is set aside.
Additional respondents 4 to 6 who are the legal representatives of the owner/2nd respondent are directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is made clear that their liability will be to the extend they inherited from the deceased 2nd respondent.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
